title: The seven mansions
hookLine: Teresa's castle has seven dwelling places, and the King lives in the center
carry: the king is in the center

lines: MANY ROOMS, AND ONE AT THE CENTER.
MANY STAY OUT IN THE COURTYARD.
cards: Later, Teresa is asked to write again, this time for her sisters. She says she didn't know how to begin.
Then a new picture came to her: the soul as a castle, made of a single diamond or very clear crystal, with many rooms, some above, some below, some to the sides.
In the very center is the main room, where the most secret things pass between God and the soul. The King lives there.

Plenty of souls, she says, stay out in the courtyard, around the outer wall, with no idea what's inside their own house. The book is The Interior Castle; you first stepped inside on day two hundred seventy-six.

teach.h: IN MY FATHER'S HOUSE ARE MANY MANSIONS.
teach.b: Teresa groups the rooms into seven dwelling places, and she took the word from Jesus. In John's Gospel he says, "In my Father's house are many mansions."
In the King James English, mansion means a dwelling place, a room to stay in, not a big house on a hill. Teresa's Spanish word is moradas, dwellings. So the seven mansions aren't seven buildings.
They're seven depths of one soul, the way rooms go further into a house.
The door of this castle, she says, is prayer and reflection: not cleverness or technique, just turning toward God honestly and paying attention.

teach.h: NOISY OUTER ROOMS, QUIETER INNER ONES.
teach.b: The outer rooms are crowded. She says snakes and vermin from outside creep in with you there: distractions, worries, the business of the day. That's no reason to stay out; it's just what the first rooms are like.

Further in, it gets quieter, and the light from the center reaches further. Prayer becomes less something you do and more something that happens to you, like yesterday's rain. In her picture, the King isn't far away.

teach.h: THE KING IS ALREADY AT THE CENTER.
teach.b: He's in the center of the soul, already. The castle is beautiful because he's in it, she says, and nothing we do can take that beauty away, though sin can cover it, like a black cloth thrown over a crystal in the sun.
The light is still shining underneath. For Teresa, the journey inward isn't a hunt for a missing God. It's coming home to the room where, she says, he has been the whole time.

how: Carmelites and others who pray in Teresa's way read The Interior Castle slowly, often with a spiritual director, and speak of prayer as a journey inward toward God dwelling at the center of the soul.

o: seven rooms of the soul, leading in toward God
seven convents Teresa founded across Spain
seven steps of penance before confession

s: Teresa's seven mansions are seven separate buildings
they're seven dwelling places in one castle, depths of one soul.
Teresa says sin destroys the castle's beauty
she compares sin to a black cloth over a crystal. the light still shines underneath.
Teresa took the word mansions from John's Gospel
in my Father's house are many mansions.

games.q: you're standing outside Teresa's castle, in the courtyard. how do you get in?
o: through the door of prayer and reflection.
wait until you're good enough to be invited.
games.why: Teresa says the door to the castle is prayer and reflection. nothing more complicated than turning toward God and paying attention.

practice: Notice where you are in Teresa's picture, out in the noisy courtyard or a first room where worries crawl in too, and don't fight it. Take one step further: one more breath of attention, one layer quieter.
If you pray, turn toward the King at the center without needing to reach him; if you don't, just notice that there's an inside, and rest there.

wordCard.voice: The seven mansions. Teresa's dwelling places of the soul, one inside another, opening toward the center, where the King lives.

carryVoice: Your line: the king is in the center. The light still shines under the cloth. Until tomorrow.
